name: Life Extension
history: Life Extension was founded in 1980 in Florida by Saul Kent and William Faloon as the non-profit Life Extension Foundation. Supplements were sold through an affiliated for-profit company, the Life Extension Foundation Buyers Club, which paid royalties to the foundation. The FDA raided its warehouse in 1987 and both founders were indicted in 1991; the company says every charge was dismissed by 1996. The foundation now operates as the Biomedical Research & Longevity Society, while the privately owned supplement business trades as Life Extension from Fort Lauderdale. It sells nearly 400 supplements, offers mail-order laboratory tests and publishes Life Extension Magazine.

positives.text: NSF's official NSF/ANSI 455-2 GMP listing (checked November 2026) includes Life Extension's operating company for its distribution facilities in New Jersey and Nevada.
The company says it will provide, on request, a summary of the contract-manufacturer and independent-laboratory test reports for every supplement it sells.
ConsumerLab's 2026 survey of supplement users rated Life Extension the top catalog/internet merchant and brand for customer satisfaction; this is a consumer survey, not a product test.

negatives.text: FDA warning letter in February 2017 said website and Facebook claims presented products as treatments for diseases such as breast cancer, and noted over 400 products with disease claims.
FDA agents raided its warehouse in 1987, and a federal indictment unsealed in 1991 accused the founders of importing unapproved drugs; the company reports all charges were dismissed by 1996.
In May 2013 the IRS revoked the Life Extension Foundation's tax-exempt status, retroactive to 2006, over its ties to the for-profit Buyers Club; the foundation challenged this in court.
